picks.excerpt: The growing use of AI large language models could make human writing, perspectives and reasoning more alike, according to a research paper that raises questions about creative diversity and authorial voice.
picks.rationale: Fresh peer-reviewed finding that LLM use flattens voice and reasoning — the single most craft-relevant research item in the pool.

picks.excerpt: GEO is generative engine optimization: trying to influence whether your name or book appears in AI overviews or in chatbot conversations, and it works differently from SEO.
picks.rationale: Directly changes how authors and publishers do discovery work tomorrow: GEO replaces SEO assumptions for AI answers.

picks.excerpt: A new app called iLands allows the creation of autonomous AI agents that not only write articles but pitch their work to media outlets.
picks.rationale: Named new tool (iLands) that pushes agents past drafting into pitching — a concrete shift in the submissions inbox.

picks.excerpt: A new interactive exhibition about the writing of James Baldwin features an AI-programmed typewriter that directs users to writing drawn from Baldwin's books, essays, and letters.
picks.rationale: A rare constructive design case: AI used as an archive interface rather than a generator, with a physical interaction to copy.

picks.excerpt: Author Daisy Buchanan argues that handing routine writing tasks such as emails to ChatGPT quietly erodes the everyday craft skills writers depend on.
picks.rationale: Working-writer argument that the cost of offloading small writing tasks shows up in the big ones — pairs with the homogenisation research.
